about.intro: Rise Against Suicide pairs youth at risk with community therapists who deliver free, short-term therapy in schools and other community settings. CU Boulder brings research expertise to help strengthen that system — starting with the therapists doing the work.

partnershipNote.text: This toolkit is built through a partnership between Rise Against Suicide and the University of Colorado Boulder.

toolkit.heading: Four Core Sections
toolkit.intro: Everything here serves one goal: reducing suicidal ideation in the youth you treat. Rather than replacing your clinical judgment or training, this toolkit is meant to give you a clear roadmap, vetted resources, guidance for working with schools, and support for your own sustainability in this rewarding, yet challenging, work — built with therapists, clinical and research experts through a Discover, Design, Build, Test process.

roadmap.heading: Treatment Planning / Roadmap
roadmap.intro: We know 12 sessions is short — that's why we built this toolkit. Developed with therapists and clinical and research experts in youth suicide prevention, the Treatment Roadmap structures our brief model around its central goal, reducing suicidal ideation, and what matters most in a short window to get there: reducing risk and stabilizing crisis, building emotion regulation, problem-solving and support-seeking skills, and building a life worth living. Click any phase below to expand it and see sample evidence-based interventions for that stage.

phases.title: Phase 2: Train & Teach Skills
interventions: DBT skills: distress tolerance & emotion regulation

phases.title: Phase 3: Consolidate & Next Steps
interventions: Warm handoff to ongoing care provider
Final screenings to measure change in suicidal ideation

schools.heading: Navigating Schools
schools.intro: We've built a school navigation page filled with resources to support your work in schools: a list of questions to ask schools to get to know the lay of the land, tips for navigating tricky interactions, and suggestions for collaborating with schools to best support youth and families.

quote.text: We're definitely navigating 50 systems every time we walk into a school.

items.body: How to navigate school partnership complexities, coordinate with counselors, and manage referrals.

items.title: District-Specific Info
items.body: Detailed guides for the schools and districts Rise frequently partners with.

items.title: Multi-System Coordination
items.body: Resources for collaborating across hospitals, clinics, and school teams.

selfcare.heading: Therapist Support & Self-Care
selfcare.intro: Working with youth at risk for suicide is some of the hardest clinical work there is. These tools help you spot burnout early, build resilience into your practice, provide tips and tricks from your peers, and let you schedule a consultation call with our licensed clinical psychologist.

items.title: Self-Care Tip Sheets
items.body: Ideas curated for and by therapists doing high-acuity work.

items.title: Therapist Stories
items.body: Videos and testimonials from therapists sharing real challenges and how they navigated them.

items.title: Pre-Session Mindfulness
items.body: Brief grounding practices to prepare for emotionally demanding sessions.

items.title: Schedule a Consultation
items.body: Book time with a clinical psychologist or Rise team member for peer support.

howToUse.heading: How Do I Use This Toolkit?
howToUse.intro: This toolkit is designed to be flexible: use what works for you, your clients, and your workflow.

steps.title: Start with the Treatment Roadmap.
steps.body: Use it to help you plan and deliver your therapy. Revisit session by session to see where you are and what comes next.

steps.title: Dip into the Treatment Library when you need something specific.
steps.body: Align it with the Roadmap, and treat it like a search tool: pull a handout for a family session, grab an assessment before intake, or find a referral when treatment is wrapping up.

steps.title: Turn to Navigating Schools before or during any school-facing work.
steps.body: Review the sample questions ahead of a school meeting, or reference the role-clarification tips when a case starts to feel tangled between systems.

steps.title: Revisit Therapist Self-Care regularly, not just when things feel hard.
steps.body: Build a check-in by integrating these tools into your own routine — weekly, monthly, whatever's sustainable — so you catch signs of strain early rather than after burnout sets in.

tips: You don't need to use every tool with every client. Pick what's relevant to the case in front of you.
Tools can be adapted. Use your clinical judgment to fit language, pacing, and content to each youth and family.
Come back often. This is meant to be a living resource you return to throughout a case, not a one-time read!
If you want support, or to talk through a case, remember you can also schedule a consultation call with our licensed clinical psychologist.

feedback.text: If you have suggestions to improve our toolkit, please let us know! The goal is to support you best — we need your help knowing how to do this.

research.heading: Discover. Design. Test.
research.intro: This toolkit is being co-designed through a rigorous, community-engaged research process with Rise therapists — not built for them, but with them.

aims.title: Discover
aims.body: Focus groups and interviews with 10 Rise therapists, analyzed across 9 domains covering strengths, challenges, interventions, and toolkit vision.

aims.title: Design & Build
aims.body: Two two-session co-design workshop sequences with Rise therapists, creating and refining toolkit prototypes based on real needs.

aims.title: Test
aims.body: Mixed-method pilot testing through interviews and surveys with community therapists to assess feasibility and acceptability.
